candidate: Resident routed-MMQ preparation reuse and Strata grouped-prefill applicability
kind: Read-only reanalysis of an existing software trace, not a fresh timing experiment

selection.remaining_tokens: Four final small-batch tokens do not use the routed-MMQ helper and are excluded.
selection.checks: Require every target helper to be followed by quantization and MMQ on the same stream; require 144 triplets per microbatch, two broadcast quantizations and one non-broadcast quantization per layer, and consistent token counts.

questions: Does the selected resident path submit per-expert host copies, waits or release events?
How much target kernel time is spent in routing helpers, routed activation quantization, routed MMQ and the intervening GLU?
What optimistic GPU-work ceiling does sharing routing maps and gate/up activation preparation provide?
Do the actual expert types fit Strata's IQ4_XS gate/up and Q2_0 or IQ4_NL down implementation?

decision.preparation_reuse: Do not implement if even the optimistic removable-work estimate is below 3% throughput-equivalent in the selected target GPU span. This is a complexity triage rule, not a measured end-to-end speed gate.
decision.optimistic_estimate: Remove two of three routing helpers and the second gate/up quantization in every layer, with zero replacement cost. Report separately the still looser removal of all routed preparation.
decision.fusion: Do not port the mismatched fused-IQ kernel or infer its performance. Record arithmetic changes and unsupported layers; a new IQ3_S kernel needs a separately scoped design and protocol.
decision.timing_limits: Use interval union for GPU busy time. CPU API durations overlap GPU execution and must not be added to kernel time. No hardware bandwidth, cache-miss, unprofiled throughput or deployment claim follows.
